summary: This is the robot pet family after the AI added a new feature: every pet class now has a speak method that returns a different sentence depending on the pet's type, its battery level, and its mood. The battery property still clamps any value into the 0-100 range, so speak can rely on it.

lines.text: Assigning to self.battery in the constructor runs the property setter, not a plain attribute assignment, so a pet created with battery=150 or battery=-5 is corrected before anything else touches it.
The setter stores the cleaned-up number in the private _battery attribute; this is where the two new unit tests for the battery bounds aim their assertions.
Charging reads the property and writes it back, which means charging past 100 is clamped for free rather than needing its own check here.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} says: 'I need to recharge...'"
lines.text: The battery check comes first in every speak method, so a tired pet says it needs charging even when its mood is happy. That ordering is the behaviour the tests need to pin down.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} says: 'Purrr! I am a happy kitty!'"
lines.text: Each subclass overrides speak with its own wording, so calling speak on a RobotCat runs the cat's version instead of the one inherited from RobotPet.
The final return is the fallback for a charged pet whose mood is anything other than "happy", so every path through speak produces a string.
